abstract: Broadband infrastructure is a crucial driver reshaping the entrepreneurial environment. Using panel data from Chinese prefecture-level cities and exploiting the quasi-natural experiment provided by the ‘Broadband China’ policy, this study employs a difference-in-differences model to identify the causal impact of broadband infrastructure on urban entrepreneurial activity. The results indicate a significant and robust positive effect, particularly in eastern cities. Mechanism analysis suggests that broadband infrastructure enhances entrepreneurship through increased venture capital investment, improved human capital, and strengthened innovation capacity. Furthermore, spatial econometric analysis reveals notable spillover effects on neighbouring cities. These findings provide empirical support for the role of digital infrastructure in fostering entrepreneurship and offer valuable insights for broadband-related policy design in developing countries.
